ORIGINAL TAKE ELEVEN V1. Build and verify a working original two-human-player browser game in connected repository mfackrell/katie. Rules are user-defined and authoritative: Start with exactly 11 stones, active player A, no winner. Legal moves take 1, 2 or 3 stones only when at least that many remain and no winner. Subtract taken stones. Player taking the last stone wins and game becomes FINISHED; otherwise alternate A/B. Illegal moves, unknown actions and post-victory takes must preserve the full state. Reset restores initial state. Persist every changed state in localStorage; reload restores in-progress and finished games and reset persists. Use a pure deterministic transition(state,action) engine separate from UI/persistence. UI with accessible Take 1, Take 2, Take 3 and Reset buttons and visible stone count, player, phase and winner. Scope ONLY app/project-pilots/take-eleven/ and tests/game-development/take-eleven.test.mjs. Test exact initial state, legal take 1/2/3, illegal moves, alternating turns, both A/B win paths, localStorage reload in progress, reload after victory, reset then reload. Use existing Next.js stack, no dependencies or credentials. Complete actual task planning, delegated development, independent review and allowed revisions; run deterministic and browser tests, produce verified PRIVATE PREVIEW only. NEVER merge the game, publish it to production, or modify unrelated files, database schema or infrastructure. Preserve original objective, saved artifacts and actual real provider and repository logs across every step. Log model, provider, stage, attempt, tokens, elapsed times, costs where available, artifact SHA, review findings, and final browser acceptance evidence. Do not mark completed without running code, verified browser proof and final independent review. Respect existing GitHub development approval gate and report any blocker precisely.
